question: On clean traces (eps 0, B = 0), does the sound active-identification line (A9: least consistent machine, rival search at every size n_min..N, shortest separating word, ID only when no rival exists up to N from the current and the start state) extend from 12 to 14 and 16 states when the rival checks reuse one incremental SAT instance per size and the action and per-case budgets are doubled, and does it carry over unchanged to a second, structurally different world family?
motivation: Observed: A9 identified 9/12 clean 12-state machines (ID+IDF 10/12, WRONG 0; v0.31.0) and A10 matched it on clean12 (ID 7/12, v0.32.0); the clean B = 0 line is the only line with a passing headline. At 16 states it finished nothing: A9 ID 0/6 (2 cases K = 64 spent, 4 unknown at the 120 s case budget or 10 s query cap; v0.31.0, mean wall 46 s per case) and A10 ID 0/6 IDU 6/6 (v0.32.0 secondary G16). Inferred: at 16 states the cost is (i) re-encoding the rival query at every size and every round from scratch and (ii) the K and case budgets, not soundness. Every result so far uses one world family (worlds_026: random strongly connected minimal Moore machines, k = 3, 2 observation bits), so generality is untested (Open)
